description: Benevolence must include cost and recipient in the submitted action. Strategy is reviewed, not forced.

generalStrategy.plan: Put cards into the hands that can create the most team value.
priorities: Give Attacks/reach to offensive allies and defense/healing to the endangered Lord or teammate.
When wounded, combine two total gifts this phase for the once-only heal; avoid wasting team resources chasing redundant healing.
Retain essential self-defense and use Influencing only with a concrete legal Attack objective and plausible Shu support.
generalStrategy.avoid: Benevolence does not draw cards. A Spy gift helps a future opponent; a Loyalist should not strengthen a likely Rebel.
generalStrategy.facing: His gifts fuel specialist allies; track recipients and disruption of the support chain.
generalStrategy.version: Classic skills in this build; ignore revised, SP, national-war and mobile-only upgrades.

sources.kind: Official strategy guide or official general introduction; advice synthesized and adapted

tactics.sequence: Form a concrete recipient-and-use plan before gifting. An offensive ally with reach can use Attack now/next turn; an endangered Lord needs defense now. Track total gifts toward the once-per-phase two-card heal and reassess after it triggers.
tactics.reserve: Keep essential self-defense and personally usable draw/control unless a recipient uses them better. Two gifts heal once; further gifts do not keep healing. Shared Shu faction is not shared identity.
tactics.workedExample: Lord Liu Bei, one Spy and one Rebel remain: default to self-preservation and enemy denial, not routine gifts to the Rebel.

priorities: Develop reach and use draw cards before deciding the burst is finished.
Concentrate repeated Attacks on a valuable enemy when exhausting their Dodge can secure a kill.

generalStrategy.plan: Commit Pindian costs only when enhanced attacks or denial pay.
priorities: Reserve a strong rank for Justice of Heaven and enough actual Attacks to exploit victory.

generalStrategy.avoid: Losing prevents Attack this turn. Do not gamble away your only useful Attack without a payoff.
generalStrategy.facing: High rank hand cards resist Pindian; a win lets him attack more and ignore distance.
generalStrategy.version: Classic skills in this build; ignore revised, SP, national-war and mobile-only upgrades.

sources.kind: Official strategy guide or official general introduction; advice synthesized and adapted

tactics.sequence: Before Pindian, count remaining usable Attacks, valuable targets and the rank you can afford. Win, then exploit extra use/targets and unlimited distance with ordinary Attacks. After each hit, reassess targets rather than preserving a stale two-target plan.
tactics.decision: Losing forbids Attack for the turn; do not risk a sure useful ordinary hit for a poor-rank gamble. When responding to enemy Pindian, preventing their burst can justify your strongest rank.
tactics.reserve: The wager card and attack fuel are separate costs. A high Attack used for Pindian cannot also be played afterward. A denial-only Pindian can be valid but should beat the alternative uses of your card.
tactics.workedExample: Only one Attack, also your highest card: spending it to win leaves no burst unless other conversion/draw is genuinely available.
